correctness.rationale: The corrected claim separates the short-edge spectral coefficient and an explicitly defined length-cycle functional from the published Berry phase. On the path the normalized first cosine on the interval of length S+ε gives limiting endpoint intensity 2/S. For the star, the cosine-leaf ansatz with hub continuity gives the pole-free determinant sin(kε)cos(ka)cos(kb)+cos(kε)sin(kS); at ε=0 this is sin(kS). Simplicity at 0 and π/S, persistence of the zero root, and uniform convergence away from these roots prove that the branch near π/S is the first positive one, including exclusion of possible cosine-pole modes. The cosines at this root are nonzero for a≠b, allowing amplitude normalization analytically; gluing the two long arms gives hub intensity (2/S)cos²(πa/S). The factor ε from the unitary scaling and integral −1/6 give the claimed coefficients, with differentiation justified by analyticity. In v1 Eq. (47), integration by parts gives −(1/4) times the integral of L(L')² E_1'(L); inserting the sinusoid proves −π² A_11/2 for that functional. The frozen attribution to the published phase convention is not correct: a real normalized simple branch along the small retraced one-length cycle gives zero Berry phase modulo 2π. The repair states precisely which functional is calculated and does not infer a full finite-rate phase. This is an analytic check, not a simulation or formal proof certificate.
